portion_doctrine: Video transcript of two Lightroom editing tutorials (film look preset + advanced masking). Core: tone curve + mask combinations are the power layer. Film aesthetic relies on slight softness (lower clarity, raise blacks) + warm HSL tweaks + specific shadow/highlight balancing. Advanced masking unlocks localized control: AI subject/sky detection + gradient softening + preset layering. Masks are now primary compositing tool (replacing Photoshop for many workflows). Refine saturation slider decouples tone curve contrast from unwanted saturation spikes. Key insight: tools in combination (tone curve + mask + HSL + color grading) beat individual sliders.
operating_rules: S-curve tone curve is foundation for film look (standard contrast)
Always lift shadows significantly on tone curve for film aesthetic
Lower highlights slightly to preserve detail (not zero)
Raise whites and blacks to reduce harshness (not pure black/white)
Lower clarity slightly for haze; raise texture slightly for sharpness
Film colors are never exact - emulate 'pastely Kodak summer' aesthetic via HSL
Mask opacity control critical: right-click > color overlay settings to reduce overlay saturation and see underlying image
AI subject/sky mask creates hard edge by default - must intersect with linear gradient to soften
Brush mask requires AUTO MASK enabled or will select background noise
Gradient masks must feather all the way out for natural transition
Hit 'O' key to toggle mask visibility for refinement verification
Luminance range intersection isolates effect to specific brightness zones
Tone curve + mask + HSL combinations unlock infinitely more control than individual sliders
Refine saturation slider decouples tone curve contrast from saturation punch (drag down to reduce spike)
Create overlay presets (mask only, no adjustments) and apply with opacity slider for variable intensity
Color point adjustment (HSL) localizes hue/sat/luminance changes to single color within mask
prompts: When editing film look: apply S-curve first, then lift shadows, then HSL warm tones
When softening image: lower clarity + lower dehaze + raise blacks, check with 'O' key
When masking auto-selection: always check for hard edges and intersect with gradient
When creating overlay preset: uncheck all adjustments, save mask only, name for reuse
When struggling with saturation spike: use refine saturation slider to dial back tone curve color punch

content_ideas: Document the 'overlay preset' pattern as reusable macro for speed (brightening_sky, center_pop, darken_foreground)
Build masking decision tree: when to use subject vs. sky vs. gradient vs. brush
Create tone curve reference chart: S-curve baseline + shadow lift + color curve warmth offsets
Test preset stacking: can 3-5 overlay presets layer without degradation?
Compare 'intersect with luminance range' vs. manual brush masking on highlight isolation
contradictions: Segment says 'lower clarity for film look' but also 'raise texture slightly' - tension between softness and detail definition. Likely resolution: clarity = overall softness, texture = microcontrast detail within soft envelope.

Segment describes HSL as 'hard to emulate exactly' (film stock variance) then provides specific HSL moves (warm reds/yellows). Tension between 'no exact method' and 'these moves work.' Likely: guidelines work within 70% accuracy but subject lighting/stock require case-by-case refinement.
weird_gold: Auto-mask on brush masking is almost throwaway mention but CRITICAL - without it, brush selects background noise and ruins the mask
Refine saturation slider is described as 'new' - decouples tone curve saturation side effect from contrast intent. Suggests Lightroom tone curve historically conflates contrast + color punch.
Mask opacity overlay is not about mask strength - it's about SEEING THROUGH the overlay to verify what's masked. Different mental model than opacity.
Object mask's secondary use: box-draw to remove overspray gaps. Not intended use but faster than manual brush cleanup.
Overlay preset system (mask only, no adjustments) is essentially saving-and-loading mask geometry as a preset - unlocks speed but requires new mental model of 'preset as shape, not settings.'
